question: does the DiT's denoised prediction move when the encoder is int8_convrot instead of bf16 pruned, and by more than an equal-sized random error
producer: bench/measure_encoder_quant_dit.py at bec97911 (capture, then forward); the forward phase was stopped by hand after violin_i2v step 8, and these rows are parsed from its log, which prints every comparison as it completes
dit: minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors (the shipped base, itself int8_convrot W8A8), ComfyUI default attention, no LoRA, no Sol
schedule: h3_config.SAMPLING simple, 16 steps, h3_config.SIGMA_SHIFT; probes at steps 0, 8 and 15 (15 for violin_t2v only)

arms.attribution: bf16 with int8's image-token rows only (zero by construction on t2v)
arms.control: bf16 plus random directions with int8's per-token error norms
arms.scale: bf16 of the prompt with ' .' appended

predictions: null is exactly 0.0 on every scene and step
violin_t2v treatment well under 1% relative L2 and below the scale (' .' edit) row
i2v and ref2va treatment larger than t2v but roughly 0.5-3% at step 0, damped because the DiT also receives the references as VAE latents identical between arms
attribution (int8 image tokens only) roughly equal to treatment on image scenes
treatment within 1.5x of the norm-matched random control; the int8-inflated violin_ref2va token is the one plausible exception
all deltas shrink from step 0 to step 15
predictions_filed_before_results.threshold: int8 error counts as specific to int8 (not just its size) when treatment exceeds 2x the control on a scene

reading: the null is exactly 0.0 at every probe: the harness is deterministic

treatment, control and scale land at the same size at every probe, on t2v and on i2v; the scale arm adds one or two tokens at the END of the prompt and leaves every earlier token's conditioning bit-identical, yet moves the prediction as much as int8's error spread over every token

so this instrument does not resolve int8's encoder error from any other SMALL conditioning change: at step 0, int8, the norm-matched control and the ' .' edit all sit in one narrow band. Over a larger range the same instrument does track size: bench/results/2026-08-27_marker_epsilon_control.json, same int8 fl2va DiT and probe steps, reads larger perturbations well above this band. So a floor plausibly sits near this band at step 0, with int8 at or under it; 'any change reads the same' holds only for changes this small. The floor itself was then confirmed by a dose-response (bench/results/2026-09-27_encoder_quant_floor.json); its cause, the int8 DiT's own activation rounding, is consistent with that record and not proven. Corrected 2026-09-27 after a read of the marker record, which had been overlooked.
on i2v the image-tokens-only arm matches the treatment, so on that scene what int8 does to the DiT is its image-token error, and it reads no larger than random noise of the same size
practical: int8's effect at the DiT is no larger than appending ' .' to the prompt
not_measured: the ref2va scenes (violin_ref2va, ref2va_dialogue), which carry the heaviest conditioning tail; stopped by owner decision as not needed for the decision
off_trajectory_caveat: Only step 0 is on a real trajectory. At a later probe the harness hands the sampler the seeded noise and the empty latent with sigmas[k:k+2], so the DiT sees sigma_k * noise, not the real x_k a render reaches there; steps 8 and 15 therefore measure sensitivity on an input no real run produces, which may inflate them. The step-0 rows are the on-trajectory reading and agree with the rest: treatment at or below the control and below the scale row on both scenes. The real x_k can be rebuilt from a full run's per-step x0 (euler, no injected noise: x_{k+1} = x_k + (s_{k+1} - s_k)(x_k - x0_k)/s_k; build_api(probe_step_x0=True) makes the twin). Raised by fastdude, 2026-09-27; bench/measure_marker_epsilon.py's one_forward, which this imports, has the same property.
